parts.note: armed suggests weaponry, but this timepiece is simply strapped to the arm

explanation.definitionFit: A timepiece worn on a strap round the lower arm is literally a timing device that is armed.

clue.text: I may enter race, and end up a wreck!

indicators.note: the letter I going into the word for race puts it inside

parts.note: to run is a race, as in a hundred-metre run

explanation.surface: A driver joins a race and finishes with a smashed-up car.
explanation.walkthrough: The I is the clue's own letter I, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruin is something wrecked or destroyed beyond repair.

definitions.meaning: laid out or displayed in order

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both laid out in order and begin a journey.

clue.text: Strange growth, a sight one may see on safari

definitions.text: sight one may see on safari

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd lump on the skin is quite a spectacle on an African trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growth' looks like a wart or tumour in the surface, yet with 'a' it is just the fodder that 'Strange' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: This African wild pig is a common animal spotted on game drives across the savanna.

clue.text: They are able to identify trite Latin quotations

definitions.meaning: labels attached to items show what they are
a tag is a hackneyed quotation, often Latin

explanation.definitionFit: Labels identify things, and stock quotations from Latin authors are also so called.

clue.text: He's about to irritate with temporary stoppages

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: taken as the letters of he's, without the apostrophe
to itch is to cause irritation

explanation.surface: A man is about to annoy everyone with short delays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'going to', but 'about' here means surrounding, and the apostrophe in He's is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitches are brief snags or interruptions that hold things up for a while.

clue.text: Filing assistant needs a hand to get to work

definitions.text: Filing assistant needs a hand to get to work

parts.words: Filing assistant needs a hand to get to work
parts.note: filing suggests office papers, but it is filing nails, and the hand is what is worked on

explanation.definitionFit: A beautician who shapes and files nails needs a client's hand to work on.

parts.note: flight can mean escaping, but here it is the course flown by a plane

explanation.definitionFit: The course an aeroplane follows through the sky is its designated route.

definitions.meaning: the steel bar that railway trains run along
a family of marsh birds including the corncrake

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a railway line's bar and a wading marsh bird.

clue.text: Delivery's not left, though one is entitled to it

parts.note: a delivery of a baby is a birth
the opposite of left is right

explanation.surface: A parcel delivery has gone astray, though the recipient is owed it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' sounds like a parcel, but it is childbirth; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An inheritance or privilege held by virtue of birth is something a person is entitled to.

indicators.note: the word sound tells us to take what follows as it is spoken

parts.note: a sighting is an observation of something

explanation.surface: A sound remark backed by a quotation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable, but it signals that the word for observation is heard, not written.
explanation.definitionFit: Quoting a source or passage is the act of referring to it, using a quote.

clue.text: A decoration so often out of place

indicators.note: letters that are out of place are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Some ornament that is so often hung in the wrong spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A festoon is a garland or chain of flowers hung in a curve as an ornament.

clue.text: Head for a beating but don't turn back

definitions.text: Head for a beating but don't turn back

parts.words: Head for a beating but don't turn back
parts.note: to head for a beating is to be about to lose, and to face is not to turn your back

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to confront likely loss, literally turning toward it rather than away.

parts.note: the stage is the world of theatre and drama
a coach directs and trains a team

explanation.surface: A theatre director lays on old-fashioned vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse-drawn coach on scheduled routes is a long-obsolete means of travel.

definitions.meaning: to name someone is to identify them

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means identifies, and the noun plural means famous people.

clue.text: Tell of dramatic happening at polling-station

definitions.meaning: to tell is to narrate or relate a story
a second count of votes when an election result is very close

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means narrate, and the noun is a fresh count of ballots in a close election.

parts.note: re means about or concerning
AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.walkthrough: 'papers' looks like newspapers, but it means sheets of paper by the ream.
explanation.definitionFit: Reams are bundles of paper sheets, or loosely large amounts of writing.

parts.note: admit means let people in, and swingers are things that swing on hinges

explanation.definitionFit: Hinged barriers that open to let people through both admit visitors and swing.

clue.text: Large family, many in jail in America

indicators.note: in places the word for many inside the word for jail

parts.note: can is American slang for a prison
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, crossword shorthand for many

explanation.surface: A big family with lots of members locked up in a US prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is an extended family group, especially in Scotland.

indicators.note: post that is sorted is put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Post is sorted and sent off to a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital city of Peru.

parts.note: to see is to understand, as in I see
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, writing done by hand

explanation.definitionFit: To seem is to appear to be so, in the same verb form.

indicators.note: put in order, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A restaurant customer has ordered some fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like a request to the waiter, but it signals rearranging the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The sardine is a small oily fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Transport that gets up speed by putting one's foot down

definitions.text: Transport that gets up speed by putting one's foot down

parts.words: Transport that gets up speed by putting one's foot down
parts.note: putting your foot down usually means accelerating a car, but here a rider pushes off the ground

explanation.definitionFit: A child's two-wheeled platform is propelled by pushing a foot against the ground.

parts.note: to play gooseberry is to be an unwanted third party with a couple, as a chaperone is; Spanish points to the old Spanish chaperone

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a gooseberry is the third person tagging along with a couple; it is not the fruit here.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna was an older woman acting as chaperone to young ladies in a Spanish household.

clue.text: Retire from the contest — not up to it?

definitions.meaning: to withdraw an entrant from a race or match
the idiom not up to the mark, below standard, uses this word

explanation.definitionFit: Withdrawing from a race is to scratch, and not good enough is not up to scratch.

clue.text: A very strong atmosphere of romance

parts.note: FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud or strong
air is the atmosphere around us

explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a romantic or sexual relationship, a romance.

indicators.note: a drunk is muddled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tipsy peer goes red in the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A florid complexion is ruddy or red-faced, the same as flushed.

definitions.meaning: a tom is a male cat, and the French for cat is this word

explanation.definitionFit: The word is English for informal talk and French for cat, as a tomcat is.

clue.text: Raise the pace for the favourites

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word reads it from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: a step is a pace

explanation.surface: Lift the pace for the leading runners.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher's pets are favourites, the people most indulged.

definitions.meaning: literally sitting in a hot bath

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being in a fix also literally describes a person soaking in a warm bath.

definitions.meaning: a curved structure spanning an opening

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both cheekily knowing and a curved span.

parts.note: to enter something is to introduce it, as an item in a record
to prise is to force open with a lever

explanation.surface: Bringing in force shows plenty of initiative.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprise means readiness to undertake new ventures, a synonym of initiative.
